An index fund buys every stock in a market index such as the S and P 500 or a total world index, so its return matches the market minus a small fee. Because most actively managed funds fail to beat their index after costs over long periods, low-cost index funds are the default choice for long-term investors. Expense ratios below a quarter of a percent matter a lot when compounded over decades. Buying regularly regardless of price is covered in [[Dollar cost averaging]].
